# JSON Schema benchmarks

**Benchmarks:** [Schema](schema.md) | [JSON Encoding](jsonString.md) | JSON Schema | [Protobuf](protobuf.md)

Sury converts in both directions: a schema you wrote becomes a JSON Schema for the other side, and a JSON Schema somebody published becomes a schema that checks values and infers types.

Measured against sury 11.0.0, zod 4.4.3, @sinclair/typebox 0.34.52, arktype 2.2.3, ajv 8.20.0.

## Features

|  | Sury | Zod | TypeBox | ArkType | Ajv |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Reads a published JSON Schema back into a schema<br><sub>the direction that lets a document from someone else check values and infer types</sub> | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌† |
| Input and output sides emit separately<br><sub>a codec's two ends are two documents: what a client sends, and what it gets back</sub> | ✅ | ✅ | ❌† | ❌† | n/a |
| Emits draft-07 as well as 2020-12 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌† | ✅ | n/a |
| Emits an OpenAPI 3.0 document<br><sub>where a nullable field is `nullable: true` rather than a type union</sub> | ✅ | ✅ | ❌† | ❌† | n/a |
| A recursive schema emits `$ref` and `$defs` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | n/a |
| A document it cannot represent is refused, not guessed<br><sub>reading `{ type: "string", $ref: "https://example.com/x" }`, whose target is not in the document</sub> | ✅ | ✅ | n/a | n/a | ✅ |

<sub>Unmarked ✅ and ❌ are probes: the call was run against that library at the version above, and the table prints what happened. † marks a cell read from the library's documentation instead.</sub>

## Performance

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DZakh/sury/benchmarks/jsonSchema-performance-dark.svg">
  <img alt="JSON Schema timings, one bar per library, remeasured on every push to main" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DZakh/sury/benchmarks/jsonSchema-performance.svg">
</picture>

<sub>Median of seven rounds per cell. Sury and Zod return the checked value, Ajv returns a boolean and leaves the value alone, so the last row is not quite the same work - it is the closest thing each library offers to the same job. TypeBox schemas are JSON Schema already, so there is nothing to time in the first row, and neither it nor ArkType reads a document written elsewhere.</sub>

<sub>Remeasured on every push to main and republished as the chart above, so a bar moves with the runner as well as with the code.</sub>

## Bundle size

|  | Sury | Zod | TypeBox | ArkType | Ajv |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Emit a JSON Schema | **10.1 kB** | 64.6 kB | 11.9 kB | 47.7 kB | n/a |
| Check values against a published document<br><sub>the JSON Schema is the input, not the output</sub> | **27.0 kB** | 64.7 kB | n/a | n/a | 36.4 kB |

<sub>The three-field schema above, bundled with esbuild, minified and gzipped. A TypeBox schema is a JSON Schema already, which is why its emit row is the smallest and why it has no row below it: `Value.Check` only understands TypeBox's own objects, not a document from elsewhere.</sub>

## Conformance

|  | Assertions | Passed | Rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JSON Schema Test Suite, draft-07<br><sub>the official corpus, run through `S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow`</sub> | 927 | 866 | 93.4% |
| JSON Schema Test Suite, 2020-12<br><sub>`$dynamicRef` and remote `$ref` are the bulk of what is left</sub> | 1299 | 974 | 75.0% |
| A converted schema converts back to itself<br><sub>`toJSONSchema` then `fromJSONSchema` then `toJSONSchema` again</sub> | 594 | 572 | 96.3% |

<sub>The suite is pinned by commit in `packages/json-schema-test-suite/suite-ref.json` and run in CI. An assertion counted as errored is a keyword `fromJSONSchemaOrThrow` refuses rather than one it gets wrong: it throws on a document it cannot represent instead of quietly accepting values the document forbids, which is why the false-accept count is 1 and not the difference.</sub>
